(Stomps Superman further into the ground, and lifts him into the air) My skin can withstand a nuclear explosion!

characters.name: The Ultimen
characters.description: A set of five super-humans who initially appear allied with the US Government. Secretly engineered artificially by Cadmus bio-engineers, the process was unstable and so their lives were drastically shortened. Consist of Downpour, Juice, Long Shadow, Shifter and Wind Dragon. Adaptational Villainy: Just like Galatea to Power Girl, Wind Dragon, Juice, Shifter, and Downpour's collectiveSanity Slippageis probably why they're not Samurai, Black Vulcan, and theWonder Twins. Animorphism: Shifter has the ability to change into different animals. Anti-Villain: The original team do end up as villains (with the exception of Long Shadow), but they're also scared kids who've just learned that they're considered expendable and are probably going to die soon. Artificial Human: They're all artificial humans created by Cadmus to be another countermeasure to the Justice League.

characters.name: Rick Flagg
characters.description: Colonel Rick Flagg, Jr. is a patriotic officer of the U.S.A who serves as the leader of Task Force X. He is the only non-criminal on the team, a talented hand-to-hand combatant, and a gifted tactician with a profound sense of duty and patriotism. Actor Allusion: This isn't the first timeAdam Baldwinplaysa high-ranking member of a shady government agency task force on otherworldly missions. Badass Normal: He has no powers, yet he can easily fight through the Watchtower.Unarmed. Blood Knight: Flagg seems to relish fighting the Justice League. Colonel Badass: Manages to go head-to-toe with the League.

characters.name: Deadshot
characters.description: Deadshot, also known as Floyd Lawton, is an assassin for hire that will take on anyone and anywhere as he has no evil agenda other than his next paycheck. He is also a member of the Task Force X. Adaptational Villainy: He was a much more nuanced figure in the comics, complete with aMorality Petin the form of his daughter. Here he's just an unusually talented hitman with no nuance, nothing more than a gun for hire. Badass Normal: Deadshot has no powers; he's just an incredibly talented marksman. Boxed Crook: As a member ofTask Force X. Cold Sniper: A master marksman with no qualms about killing.

characters.name: Plastique
characters.description: A crook with a knack for explosives, recruited into Task Force X. Adaptational Superpower Change: In the comics, she was a metahuman with the power to explode things. Here, she's just an explosives expert. Beauty Is Never Tarnished: Averted. Deadshot sets off the grenade she was holding to serve as a distraction for the rest of the team to escape, and Captain Atom is too late to pull her away before she takes the brunt of the explosion.We don't get to see her afterwards, but if Cap's reaction is any indication, it ain't pretty. Big "NO!": When one of the Watchtower's shield doors seemingly shuts on her and Deadshot. Fortunately for them, Captain Atom was there to save the day. Gory Discretion Shot: She's horribly disfigured by one of her own explosives, but she's covered by the bomb's smoke and we only see Captain Atom's horrified reaction to seeing her.

characters.name: Captain Boomerang
characters.description: A supervillain who performs robberies with high tech boomerang gadgets. He was a member of Task Force X until Cadmus was overhauled. Battle Boomerang: Captain Boomerang gets his name from using specialized boomerangs as weapons. Boxed Crook: Captain Boomerang agrees to go on suicide missions with Task Force X rather than be executed in the chair. He finishes his service by the time of "Flash and Substance". Even Evil Has Standards: Captain Boomerang's done enough to warrant the death sentence and he's perfectly fine with leaving his Task Force X teammates to fend for themselves if it means he gets away. However, it's implied by his expression when Flagg gives Deadshot a well-deserved beatdown that even he was disgusted by Deadshot causing Plastique to be caught in an explosion to ensure his escape. Offscreen Villain Dark Matter: Averted with Captain Boomerang who's always pleading poverty because his special boomerangs and deathtraps are expensive.

characters.name: Clock King
characters.description: Temple Fugate, also known as the Clock King, was an efficiency expert with a grudge against Mayor Hill. He's later recruited into Task Force X.

characters.name: Maxwell Lord
characters.description: Maxwell Lord serves as the manager and public face of the Ultimen, and is less involved with the gritty missions of Cadmus as compared to most officers and agents. Adaptational Heroism: Retroactively. "Ultimatum" aired months beforeCountdown toInfinite Crisissaw print, and was hence based on his earlier characterization as a somewhat sleazy but at worst morally grey person, rather than his outright dyed-in-the-wool supervillain portrayal fromIConward. While he is complicit in the Ultimen operation, it's only as a team manager and PR consultant. Adaptational Wimp: The comic book version of Maxwell Lord was a powerful psychic — this version appears completely human. Everyone Has Standards: He may be slimy and money-grubbing but he does genuinely care about the Ultimen, wanting them to live out their shortened lives in comfort. When the team goes rogue, he agrees to find them after Waller says the alternative is her giving the order to have them killed. The Handler: He serves as this to the Ultimen, getting the team to follow Cadmus' instructions without revealing the groups' origins or true purpose.

characters.name: Vance
characters.description: An agent of Cadmus undercover as a Watchtower technician. Call-Forward:Word of Godis that he's the son of Robert Vance, theVillain of the WeekofBatman Beyond's "Lost Soul". The Dog Was the Mastermind: He's an unassuming background character who turns out to have been essential to Task Force X's heist of the Watchtower. Karma Houdini: "Lost Soul" reveals he became CEO of his father's company, meaning he was wealthy and powerful for years after the Watchtower heist with no indication he faced any punishment. Killed Offscreen: He dies prior to "Lost Soul" from a heart attack.

characters.name: Secret Society
characters.description: A supervillain team formed by Grodd. The team's original purpose was forming a cohesive unit to destroy the original Justice League. Failing in this endeavor, Grodd expanded his society as a direct response to the Justice League expanding its own membership. The second iteration acted more as a protection racket for supervillains, allowing individual members to pursue their own agendas and receive support from the Secret Society in exchange for a cut of the profit on any criminal enterprises. Adaptation Name Change: The group is called the Secret Society instead of The Legion of Doom. The Justice League was originally going to refer to them as the latter only for it to be quashed by executives. Composite Character: In the last season ofJLU, the Society was, for all intends and purposes,the Legion of Doom, but due toExecutive Meddling, it was still called the Secret Society in the show itself. Disappointed by the Motive: All of them are disappointed to find out Grodd's master plan was to turn everyone on Earth into apes. None of them lift a finger in opposition when Luthor shoots him and usurps control and the only reason so many end up rejoining Grodd and turning against Luthor is because Luthor was acting crazy and being even more of aBad Bossthan usual. Dwindling Party: By the final season ofUnlimitedit includes nearly every villain of the DCAU. Unfortunately, by the finale, only a handful are left after the villain civil war and subsequent battle with Darkseid. Not even the leaders Grodd or Lex made it.

characters.name: Gorilla Grodd
characters.description: A mastermind gorilla from Gorilla City, a place where many hyper-intelligent gorillas live. After being ousted for his experiments in mind control, he turns to full-time villainy in order to gain wealth and resources to continue his research. He is most notable for organizing a number of villainous alliances to counter the Justice League. Adaptational Nice Guy: While firmly on the villain side, Grodd is much less evil than his comic book counterpart and most versions. He treats his subjects with decency, making the Secret Society into abig happy family, and while he still hasFantastic Racismtowards humans, he largely outgrows it. His ultimate plan changes fromKill All Humanstoturn everyone in the world to apes, which is more goofy than straight-up genocidal. Adaptational Jerkass: On the other hand, Grodd hates Gorilla City much more than his comic counterpart. Usually Grodd's ambitions are to rule over the city and lead an army against mankind, being a radical ape revolutionary. While he has led attacks on it's people, he still doesn't want to destroy his home. His first episode here has him try to nuke Gorilla City to rubble out of spite that he can't rule. Affably Evil: After someCharacter Development, heevolvesinto this. Animal Is the New Man: It turns out Grodd never fully got over his idea that gorillas should be the dominant species on the planet, as his master plan inUnlimitedwas to turn every single human into a gorilla.

characters.name: Lex Luthor
characters.description: A genius multi-billionaire living in Metropolis who is the chief executive of his own company,LexCorp. In reality, he's a sociopath with a thirst for power and control, which he will gladly go to any length to have. Constantly flexes hisVillain with Good Publicitymuscle as much as he possibly can and has the resources and connections to finance and direct plots against Superman from a distance while still appearing as a benign, philanthropic captain of industry to the public at large. He's an A-lister among Superman's rogues, not bad for a guy who doesn't have any superpowers and has to share a city with the originalFlying Brick. He later takes on various exploits to hamper theJustice Leagueand out them as threats to global security so he may do as he pleases unopposed. In addition to funding and exploiting Cadmus, he later becomes a member, then leader of the secondSecret Society.

characters.name: Sinestro
characters.description: A disgraced former member of the Green Lantern Corps, he was a personal nemesis to John Stewart.

characters.name: Giganta
characters.description: Giganta was a super villain with the ability to increase or decrease her size at will. She befriended Grodd and became a member of his Secret Society. Adaptational Personality Change: This version is much more feminine than her comics counterpart. Adaptational Modesty: This version wears a dress instead of a leopard-spotted loincloth and top, and wears shoes. Amazonian Beauty: She's more buff than Wonder Woman and just as attractive. Anti-Villain: While undoubtedly a villain, Giganta doesn't go out of her way toKick the Dogand seems to be among the most human of the Society's members. She joins the society out of devotion to Grodd and no other reason.

characters.name: Killer Frost
characters.description: Killer Frost was a super-villainess who had the ability of Cryokinesis and was a member of Grodd's Legion of Doom. Adaptational Modesty: A slight example. This version of Killer Frost wears a unitard instead of aleotard. Adaptational Ugliness: Many versions of Frost are often depicted as seductive femme fatales with the allure of an ice princess, but this incarnation of the Killer looks borderlinedemonic. Ambiguous Situation: There’s been three Killer Frosts in the comics, but it’s never clarified which one this Frost is supposed to be. Ax-Crazy: The girl likes murdering.

characters.name: Shade
characters.description: Shade was a supervillain who controlled shadows. He joined a record number of four separate Anti-Justice League organizations. Adaptational Ugliness: He's much oldernoteWell,physicallyand uglier in the DCAU than he is in the comics. Adaptational Villainy: While he was a villain in the comics for a long time, by the time theJustice Leagueanimation was running he had become anAnti-Hero, a characterisation that has largely stuck. Adaptational Wimp: Shade here was based on the pre-Robinson version and thus didn't seem to be near as powerful as his post-Zero Hour counterpart, who was strong enough to defeat severalBlack Lanternswith relative ease. Amazon Chaser: He's not the least bit bothered by Giganta being aStatuesque Stunner, in fact helikesit. Even after learning she used to be a gorilla. Then there's his reaction to seeing her gigantism power in action.Shade:This just gets better and better.

characters.name: Parasite
characters.description: Once an employee of S.T.A.R. Labs, Rudy was exposed to an experimental chemical compound that spilled on him when he tried to steal it. Now, as the Parasite, he possesses the power to absorb the energy, memories and physical abilities from anyone he touches, including Superman. He later joins theSecret SocietyinJustice League.

characters.name: Clayface
characters.description: An actor indebted to Roland Daggett in exchange for a supply of "Renuyu", a formula that is able to remold facial features, which Hagen relied on to mask the damage done to his face following a bad accident. When Daggett wanted to end their "business relationship" on less-than-amicable terms, his hired muscle attempted to kill Hagen by over-exposing him to Renuyu. However the effect of the substance wound up changing him into a shapeshifting monster.

characters.name: Devil Ray
characters.description: He is also known as Black Manta, but was renamed in the show due tothe Aquaman Embargo. Accidental Murder: When Deadman sees that he's recovered and is about to shoot Wonder Woman from behind, Deadman possesses Batman and shoots him with a gun lying on the ground, which causes Devil Ray to stumble back into an exposed electrical panel. Adaptation Name Change: He's Black Manta, but DC placed an embargo onAquamancharacters due to planning anAquamanshow andnot wanting children to get confused by two versions of the same character. Black Manta was allowed to appear inUnlimited, but had to be renamed. Arch-Enemy: He seems to treat Wonder Woman as his rival and is eager to kill her the most. Asshole Victim: Considering he's a gleeful murderer who slaughtered an entire village of peaceful monks, it's safe to say no tears were shed when Deadman accidentally murders him horribly. Even Batman is probably more upset that Deadman’s possession of him led to Devil Ray’s death than upset that Devil Ray died.

characters.name: Doctor Polaris
characters.description: A supervillain with magnetic powers who accompanies Luthor on his initiation mission for the Secret Society. Once Luthor usurps Grodd, Polaris chafes under his unstable leadership and attempts to perform a coup of his own. Ambiguous Situation: There are two villains in the comics who have used the name Doctor Polaris, Neal Emerson and John Nichols. It’s never clarified which one this Doctor Polaris is supposed to be. Ambition Is Evil: He's a nakedly ambitious supervillain who wants to take over the Secret Society from Lex Luthor. Deadpan Snarker: He's usually more abrasive than sarcastic but he does have his moments of dry wit.Chuck:Whoever you guys are, you've got no business being here.Doctor Polaris:Sorta goes with the territory—we're thieves. Even Evil Has Standards: Played for laughs. He may be a murderous, scheming supervillain but even Doctor Polaris is disgusted when Luthor—really the Flash in Luthor's body—uses the bathroom without washing his hands.Doctor Polaris:You gonna wash your hands?Flash-as-Luthor:No.Cuz I'm evil!

characters.name: Atomic Skull
characters.description: Atomic Skull is a supervillain who is a member of the Legion of Doom. Adaptational Wimp: He's one of Superman's foes in the comics, with the power to back it up. In theDCAU, he still has superpowers but aBadass Normallike Wildcat can severely trounce him in a physical fight. However, Lex Luthor gives him some power augmentations later on as seen in “To Another Shore”, reducing this somewhat. Affably Evil: In spite of his fearsome appearance, Atomic Skull is unfailingly polite for a supervillain and one of the more sympathetic members of the Secret Society. In the final episode, he is one of the first characters to propose an alliance with the Justice League and saves Shayera's life out of his own free will. Atomic Superpower: His main superpower is firing concentrated blasts of radiation. Badass on Paper: Was the champion of the Meta-Brawl and touted as a tough fighter but all of his appearance involve him getting his butt kicked. Only time he is shown to win a fight is the series finale.

characters.name: Cheetah
characters.description: Cheetah was a former scientist turned into a supervillain after genetically modifying herself. She was a member of the Injustice Gang and Legion of Doom. Adaptational Backstory Change: Apart from her appearance, she has almostnothingin common with any of her comic-book counterparts; the one she's closest to, Barbara Minerva, was atomb-robbingEnglish noblewoman who became a werecat through amagicalritual and wasa dedicated enemy of Wonder Woman. Adaptational Nationality:If we take her origin from the tie-in comics into accountand this incarnation of Cheetahisintended to be Barbara Minerva, then this technically counts. In theWonder Womancomics, she originally hailed from England. Here, she is voiced by Sheryl Lee Ralph, who uses her natural American accent. Adaptational Nice Guy: Minerva was originally a straight-upAxe-CrazyBlood Knightwho cherished the thrill of hunting and embraced her wild side, while this incarnation of Cheetah is a borderlineTragic Villainwho's only vile for the money, displays some regret in killing people, and despises her mutation with a passion. Adaptational Wimp: Minor example. Cheetah's a savage fighter but she does not possess great super speed. Most of her counterparts are so fast they can actually keep up withthe Flash, but this version simply has quick reflexes.It's more evident with her constant defeats against Wonder Woman that lasts seconds before she is knocked out.

characters.name: Star Sapphire
characters.description: Star Sapphire is a villain that is for hire and a member of the Injustice Gang and Legion of Doom. Adaptational Nationality: She's been changed from American toBritish. Adaptational Villainy: She went from anAnti-Heroto a full on villain. Alpha Bitch: While not explicitly stated to be a queen like in the comics, she sure is haughty enough. When she finds that she wasn't the only supervillain summoned by Luthor to join his Injustice Gang, she snidely asks if she's been reduced to being in the ranks of "common criminals" now. Ambiguous Situation:Word of Godhas confirmed that she's supposed to be Carol Ferris. Since untilJustice League vs. The Fatal Five, it seemed Hal wasn't a Green Lantern in this continuity, what led to her becoming a Star Sapphire is unknown. If anything, she genuinely believed in Aresia's cause to eradicate all men because of her past experience with some "very unpleasant men [she's] known over the years."

characters.name: Copperhead
characters.description: A dimwitted snake-like supervillain-for-hire. Abhorrent Admirer: When he first meets Cheetah, he tries to flirt with her by flicking his forked tongue at her. She understandably responds by slashing him with her claws. Butt-Monkey: He never comes out on top in any of his appearances. Deadpan Snarker: Whenever he gets partnered up with Solomon Grundy. Demoted to Extra: He was a more prominent supporting villain inJustice Leaguebut by the time ofJLU, he has only one speaking role in "Kid Stuff" and a small handful of non-speaking cameo appearances throughout the rest of that iteration.

characters.name: Roulette
characters.description: Roulette was a conniving entrepreneur who ran an illegal, no-halt, cage fighting league called the Meta-Brawl. Badass Normal: Roulette had no powers of her own, but she was endowed with a keen intellect, and surrounded herself with all sorts of security gimmicks, such as death traps and robot security dogs. Cleavage Window: Ironically, her comic book counterpart had the same window on her dress, just a bit lower. Combat Commentator: A villainous example as she provides color commentary for Meta-Brawls, and, later, for the Glamor Slam. Dark Action Girl: Huntress assumes Roulette's just the type to sit on the sidelines while others do her dirty work. She's surprised when Roulette proves she can go toe to toe with her, even if Roulette ends up losing their fight.

characters.name: Doctor Destiny
characters.description: Doctor Destiny is the alter ego of John Dee, a low life convict who acquired the ability of ESP. Adaptational Dumbass: The Dee of the show is a petty criminal who volunteered for experiments with the Materioptikon. The Dee of the comics was aMad Scientistwho (putting aside the power source turning out to beMorpheus's dreamstone) built the Materioptikon himself. And I Must Scream: What he usually inflicts on his victims, and later on the receiving end whenhe accidentally drugs himself in his fight with Batman, essentially lobotomizing himself as his powers trap him in his mind,humming "Frère Jacques" foreverwith little awareness of the outside world. He seems to recover by the start of the fifth season, appearing as a member of the new Secret Society, but as this was supposedly an animation error, it's highly likely he's still suffering his aforementioned fate. Arc Villain: For "Only A Dream". Ascended Fanboy: Dee is first seen as a nobody inmate fantasizing about being accepted by major supervillains like Lex Luthor and the Joker. Come the final season ofUnlimitedand he's gotten his wish as a member of the new Secret Society.

characters.name: Tsukuri
characters.description: A mercenary who served Aresia as a member of the second Injustice Gang. She later became a member of the second Secret Society. Adaptational Villainy: She's an assassin and accessory to Aresia's attemptedgendercidethat's loosely based onKatana. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: When their plane starts to go down, she grabs a jetpack and abandons Aresia. What Happened to the Mouse?: She makes a cameo in "Dead Reckoning" as a member of Grodd's Legion of Doom and then is never seen again.

characters.name: Bizarro
characters.description: An imperfect clone of Superman created by Luthor. He has almost all of Superman's strengths, but a damaged mind that leaves him unable to think clearly and understand that his actions are harmful. He truly wants to be a hero, but doesn't understand that he's actually hurting people. A while afterwards, Luthor lobotomizes and brainwashes him in order to be more evil, and he becomes part of theSecret Society.

characters.name: Toyman
characters.description: Winslow Schott wanted nothing more in life than to make toys. Unfortunately, he had little money, and could only achieve his dream by taking a loan from gangster Bruno Mannheim. The toy company soon became a front for Intergang activities. When the police busted the operation, Mannheim let Winslow take the fall, and the kindly toymaker spent the rest of his life in prison. Now Schott's son seeks revenge, adopting the identity of Toyman and using a variety of deadly toy-themed weapons anddeath trapsagainst the gangster and his mooks. Naturally, this attracts Superman's attention. He later joins theSecret SocietyinJustice League Unlimited.

characters.name: Metallo
characters.description: John Corben was a mercenary hired byLexCorptostealan experimentalMini-Mechaand deliver it to Lex's (illegal) buyers. Superman's debut in Metropolis was crushing the robot and hauling Corben off to prison. While in jail, Corben contracted a fatal disease. Lex Luthor, thankful for Corben refusing to testify against him, offered a solution: upload Corbin's mind into an immortal robot body, powered by a Kryptonite core. Corben enjoyed the limitless strength and durability, but the lack of touch, smell and taste drove him insane. Especially once he found out that the fatal disease he contracted was deliberately applied to himbyLuthor. Still, he is a dedicated enemy of Superman. He later joins theSecret SocietyinJustice League Unlimited.

characters.name: Mirror Master
characters.description: A supervillain who specializes in using mirrors to attack and create illusions. Adaptational Nationality: This continuity's Mirror Master is the EvanMcCullochversion according tothe tie-in comic, but noticeably speaks in an American accent rather than a Scottish one. Blaming the Victim: He says it's the Flash's own fault that Mirror Master has to kill him because the Flash would never look the other way every once in a while to let him get away with his crimes. Literally Shattered Lives: Mirror Master suffers from this when he tries to escape into a mirror, only for Batman to shatter it before he can reach the other side of the portal. Master of Illusion: Mirror Master crafts illusions with his mirrors.

characters.name: The Imperium Leader
characters.description: The supreme intelligence and ruler of the Imperium invaders. Arc Villain: He's the main villains of the three-part series premiere "Secret Origins". Bad Boss: When his agent impersonating Senator Carter clings to him and pleads to be taken with the Leader during his retreat, he simply kills him by swatting Carter off of him and into a beam of sunlight that melts him. Blob Monster: Unlike the rest of his kind, he doesn't have a humanoid shape, looking more like a giant gelatinous amoeba with tentacles. He even attempts to kill J'onn by absorbing him into his body. Dark Is Evil: Unlike the white and black color palettes of the rest of the Imperium, the Leader is mostly black and gray with purple outlines.

characters.name: "J. Allen Carter"
characters.description: An Imperium agent who took on the identity of astronaut J. Allen Carter. He became a Senator on Earth and used his position to help pave the way for the Imperium's invasion. Big "NO!": His last words as his leader abandons him and he dissolves into a puddle in sunlight. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: While undercover he poses as a well-meaning man who only wants to do what's best to protect the Earth from nuclear war. In reality, he's a smug sadistic agent of the Imperium who used his benign reputation to weaken the Earth so the Imperium could conquer it. Deep Cover Agent: The most prominent one among his people, as his status as a United Nations Senator allowed him to convince other countries to engage in nuclear disarmament, leaving the Earth ill-prepared to fight off the Imperium's invasion. The Dragon: Senator "J. Allen Carter" turns out to be this for the Imperium's leader. He's really a member of the species who took the place of the real J. Allen Carter and sabotaged Earth's defenses to make it easier for his species to conquer.

characters.name: Hro Talak
characters.description: A Thanagarian general and Shayera's fiancee. Adaptational Villainy: Hro Talak's willingness to blow up the Earth to help Thanagar iswhy he's not Katar Hol. Anti-Villain: Hro is an honorable man only trying to do what is best for his people. The trouble is that he's completely unwilling to come up with any kind of compromise, nor moral enough toTake a Third Option(as noted by Shayera). Arc Villain: As the head of the Thanagarian operation on Earth, he's the main villain of the three part finale, "Starcrossed". This also makes him theFinal BossofJustice Leaguebefore it transitions toUnlimited. Being Tortured Makes You Evil: He spent years being tortured in Gordanian prison camps, gaining a disfiguring scar across his face, and the harsh treatment he endured has clearly taken a toll on his sanity as he's willing to wipe out innocent planets if it means Thanagar winning the war against the Gordanians.

characters.name: Kragger
characters.description: Talak's second-in-command. Ambiguously Gay: Kragger quite visibly dislikes the reignited sparks between Hro and Shayera, takingmultiple opportunities to interfere with their relationship. When he returns inUnlimited, he's specifically angry at Shayera for "taking" Hro.Bruce Timmoutright describes Kragger as believing there's "a little more" between him and Hro than just subordinate and leader. Avenging the Villain: He returns in "Hunter's Moon" to get revenge on Shayera for her betrayal inadvertently led toThanagar losing the war against the Gordanians and Hro Talak's death. Due to the mental impairments he suffered during the events of "Starcrossed" and his (very strongly implied) sexual jealousy of Hro Talak’s love for Shayera, it's very easy for Paran Dul to convince him Shayera is to blame for everything. Butt-Monkey: He's constantly getting chewed out either verbally or physically by Shayera and Hro. He eventually ends upin a state of catatonia after Martian Manhunter forcefully reads his mind. By "Hunter's Moon" it's shown that this had some kind of permanent mental damage, confining him to a mechanized suit and leaving him in severe pain if he thinks too much, with him dying at the end of the episode when Shayera destroys said suit. Co-Dragons: He and Paran Dul serve as this to Hro Talak. Kragger may be the official second-in-command of Talak's forces but Paran Dul's work on the Hyperspace Portal is essential to Talak's strategy to defeat the Gordanians.

characters.name: Paran Dul
characters.description: Talak's lieutenant, and the chief-engineer in charge of the construction of the Hysperspace Portal. Avenging the Villain: In "Hunter's Moon" she wants to kill Shayera since her betrayal lead tothe Gordanians winning the war against Thanagar and directly resulted in Hro Talak's death, even if Talak's plans to win the war would've necessitated Earth's destruction. Canon Foreigner: Created exclusively for the series. Co-Dragons: She and Kragger serve as this to Hro Talak. While Kragger is the brawn in charge of military operations as Talak's second-in-command, Paran Dul is the brains responsible for building the Hyperspace Portal that's critical for the Thanagarians' plans. Dragon Ascendant: She returns as the main villain leading the surviving Thanagarian soldiers in "Hunter's Moon" against Shayera. Technically Kragger was Hro Talak'sDragoninstead of her, but due to the permanent mental impairments he suffered during "Starcrossed", he becomes Paran's willing subordinate.

characters.name: Brainiac
characters.description: A supercomputer from the planet Krypton who survived the planet's destruction. Now Brainiac seeks to gain as much knowledge from the galaxy as it can, by any means, as well as increase the value of that information by destroying any "redundant" data (i.e., the original civilizations).

characters.name: Mongul
characters.description: The cruel dictator of War World. He gains amusement from watching others fight in his arena, which he captures from around the galaxy to become gladiator slaves. He is deposed by Superman following his experience on War World but comes to Earth later in order to have his revenge against the Man of Steel. Adapted Out: The gem on Mongul's chest which can fire disintegration blasts that he had in the comic books isn't included in hisDCAUincarnation. Adaptational Dumbass: In anEvil Cannot Comprehend Goodway. In the original comic, he was able to correctly deduce that Superman's greatest desire would be a humble and peaceful life (although slightly wrong on the details). Here, he's unable to comprehend that Superman's greatest desire might be anything but be the bloody conquest of his enemies. Adaptational Jerkass: In the original version of "For The Man Who Has Everything", he muses (albeit mockingly) that Superman might be dreaming of a peaceful idyllic life thanks to the Black Mercy. In this version, hedoesn't even consider that a possibility, assuming that Superman could only be satisfied by conquering the universe, because that's exactly what someone like Mongul would want. Also, while he makes several sexist comments towards Wonder Woman in the comic, that aspect ismore heavily emphasized here. Amazing Technicolor Population: The color of his skin is sickly pale yellow.

characters.name: Despero
characters.description: Despero was once a Kalanorian exile due to his third eye, who, after encountering the Flame of Py'tar, became ruler of Kalanor and built an empire, bent on galactic conquest. Only through the intervention of the Justice League and theGreen LanternCorps were his plans halted. Adaptational Dye-Job: Despero's skin color in the comics had a pink-orange shade. In this series, his skin color was changed into a shade of purple in order to differentiate him from Katma Tui. Adaptational Wimp: Believe it or not, in spite of his great power here, he's this compared to his comic book counterpart who was able to battle the likes of Superman, Wonder Woman, Captain Marvel, and Power Girl all at the same time and manhandle all of them at once. In the show, a single Green Lantern like John Stewart can injure him and give him a more-or-less even fight. All of the Other Reindeer: His backstory before he became a conquering prophet. His third eye in the middle of his forehead is what sets him apart from the rest of his kind. Bad Boss: He sends one of his lieutenants out into the desert for his failure to capture the rebels without any supplies in the false hopes that he'll be welcomed back later with a vision from Despero. Shortly afterwards, it turns out Despero has no intention of allowing that lieutenant to ever return alive.

characters.name: Draaga
characters.description: Draaga was once the undefeated champion of War World. Adaptation Dye-Job: In the comics, his skin was green, but here, it's grey. Adaptational Ugliness: While the comic Draaga was never a looker, this Draaga isCovered with Scars, including burning an "S" onto his chest (in the comics, he simply wore one of Clark's shirts that he'd found). Alien Blood: What little is seen of Draaga's when he is beaten is green in colouration. Anti-Villain: Type IV. He only kills his enemies to ensure he had a homeworld and the only reason he wants revenge on Superman is due to a conflicting code of honour.

characters.name: The Manhunters
characters.description: Robots created by the Guardians of the Universe for the purpose of serving as galactic peacekeepers. Realizing their creations were suboptimal for the role they were originally designed for, the Guardians instead assigned them to lesser duties and instated the Green Lantern Corps to be their new peacekeepers. The Manhunters did not take this as well as the Guardians initially assumed. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: The Guardians' claim that the Manhunters robotic nature prevented them from grasping the subtleties and nuance between good and evil, which is why they had them reprogrammed for lesser duties and replaced by the Green Lanterns. This eventually led to the Manhunters deciding to revolt over the "insult" of being replaced by taking the Green Lanterns' powers for themselves. Badass Creed: They have a simple but effective one, "No man escapes the manhunters." Be Careful What You Wish For: The lead Manhunter wanted the Green Lanterns' power for himself. He got it by becoming one with it. Unfortunately for him, by becoming the very power he sought, he became just as susceptible to being absorbed by a Green Lantern like John Stewart. Black-and-White Insanity: The Guardians claim that this was the Manhunters main problem when they served as peacekeepers, that they "couldn't understand the subtle gradations between good and evil".

characters.name: The Justice Lords
characters.description: The counterparts of the Justice League in an alternate universe, the history of their universe was mostly the same as the history of the League's universe, but in the Lords' universe, President of the United StatesLex LuthormurderedThe Flashand almost brought the world to nuclear war.Supermansimply decided to kill Luthor, and his experience with killing caused him to unleash a totalitarian brand of justice on their Earth, completely eliminating all crime and establishing world peace at the cost of countless personal and political freedoms. Lord Batman then built a dimensional portal in his lengthy spare time, discovering the League's universe, with the Lords trying to go to this universe and unleash their totalitarian rule there. Anti-Villain: They want to make the world a safe place, but they have become totalitarian dictators in the process. Apologetic Attacker: Lord Martian Manhunter apologizes to the Justice League after luring them into a trap where he and his comrades can incapacitate and imprison them. Arc Villain: They serve as this for the two-parter "A Better World" though their existence ends up influencing the plot intoUnlimited, long after their only appearance inJustice League. Asskicking Leads to Leadership: Considering they first took command over the world by murdering the president. Lord Batman makes a military general follow his orders.

characters.name: President Lex Luthor
characters.description: Lex Luthor's counterpart in the Justice Lords' universe, who became President of the United States, killed this universe's Flash and was killed himself by Superman's heat vision. Bullying a Dragon: He taunts Superman over his unwillingness to use lethal force, which backfires on himhardwhen Superman concedes that letting him live will just allow Luthor to continue causing problems and summarily uses his heat vision to kill Luthor. Gory Discretion Shot: We don't actually see Lex Luthor's demise or his charred remains, but the scene cutting away as Superman's eyes start glowing, Batman commenting on the smell and Batman and Wonder Woman reacting to the aftermath of Superman's action upon entering the Oval Office is all the proof we need that Superman used his heat vision to kill Luthor. Hero Killer: He killed this universe's Flash. President Evil: He's become President of the United States and, aside from causing the Flash's death, is confronted by Superman over almost starting a devastating war.

characters.name: The Joker
characters.description: Batman's former enemy, now the lobotomized caretaker of Arkham Asylum. Affably Evil: He's polite and calm towards the Justice League, despite working for the Justice Lords. Bluff the Imposter: He asks Martian Manhunter for the password to the Asylum's security door. Although the password given is correct, the Joker revealsWonder Womanwas supposed to say it. Good Is Dumb: Subverted on both counts. Though affable, he is a minion of the Justice Lords. And as it turns out, while the lobotomy did change his personality, his mind is just as sharp as ever, as shown by him tricking the Justice League into giving themselves away. Heel–Face Brainwashing: After getting lobotomized, he's become the (relatively) harmless secretary for Arkham Asylum.

characters.name: Injustice Guild
characters.description: A villain team opposed to the Justice Guild, a superhero team from an alternate universe. Alliterative Name:MusicMaster andSirSwami. Disc-One Final Boss: The "Legends" two-parter initially sets them up as the central threat, but they're quickly beaten by the Justice Guild. The dark truth of the Justice Guild's universe is discovered by the Justice League and Ray Thompson is revealed to be the real threat. Evil Redhead: Music Master is a villain with red hair. Expy: Just like the Justice Guild are stand-ins for the Golden AgeJustice Society of America, the Injustice Guild are an obvious pastiche of the Justice Society's corresponding villain team the Injustice Society, with their members being based off specific Golden Age DC supervillains.Music Master is based on the Golden Age Flash villain the Fiddler, albeit younger and using an accordion as his weapon/musical instrument rather than a fiddle.Sir Swami is essentially the Wizard wearing a turban instead of a top hat.The Sportsman is an obvious stand-in for the Sportsmaster.Dr. Blizzard is based on the Alan Scott Green Lantern villain the Icicle, with his freeze rays being blasted from a doctor's head mirror rather than a gun.

characters.name: Ray Thompson
characters.description: The formerKid Sidekickof the Justice Guild, a superhero team from an alternate universe. A nuclear holocaust destroyed his world and his heroes forty years ago, but the fallout gave himPsychic Powersso powerful they allowed him towarp realityto recreate an ultra-perfect illusion of his city at the height of his childhood, before everything went to hell. Alas, Poor Villain: While he forced the other survivors to act out mundane roles for 40 years instead of rebuilding, which the ice-cream man said was like a nightmare, he's also a child who lost everything during a nuclear holocaust and tried to recreate the world of his long-gone childhood with his newfound powers. The Justice League expressSympathy for the Devilafter learning about his frankly tragic life. Ambiguous Situation: After his defeat, it's not exactly clear if he's been killed by the strain from keeping the illusion and combat, or if he's been thrown into a coma or is merely unconscious. Anti-Villain: Type 2. Ray isn't so much evil as having long sinceJumped Off the Slippery Slopedue tosuffering something no child should ever go through, and losing his idols at the same time, leaving him with no support. He did force the other survivors into playing along in his fantasy instead of rebuilding, but that could be explained by his being both too young and immature to realize that rebuilding was the better option, and insane due to his trauma. Body Horror: His true appearance is that of a hideously deformed mutant; including a disproportionately large, bulbous head and an elongated left arm,all a result of exposure to nuclear radiation.

characters.name: Ares
characters.description: The Greek god of war. He has little regard for mortals and feels their only purpose is to kill each other for his amusement. Adaptational Wimp: The iconic DC Comics version of Ares is an insanely powerful god in badass black armor who can throw the whole world into chaos and is dignified and honorable. This version is an underhanded and spiteful pretty boy that chooses to strictly act behind the scenes and flees when his plans go awry. It may be justified asAres traditionally needs to feed on conflict to be at the top of his gameand it's clear that he's practically starving from a lack of good conflict to draw from. As Long as There Is Evil: He's only mildly annoyed when Wonder Woman, Hawk, and Dove managed to talk two factions out of going to war, saying that as long asanyone elsefeels enough hatred, he'll always be around.Ares:Wherever there's prejudice, ignorance, inequality. I'll be there. Ax-Crazy: To the point he actuallyspitson people while going on his evil rants. This version of Ares is angry, violent, short-sighted and goes berserk (and sometimes murderous) when his plans go even slightly wrong. Decomposite Character: All of his comic book counterpart's more admirable qualities went to the show's version of Hades.

characters.name: Hades
characters.description: Hades is the Olympian God of the Underworld. Adaptational Backstory Change: SeeAdaptational Villainybelow. In the original myths, he fought on the side of the Greeks in the Titanomachy and became ruler of the dead because he drew the shortest straw among his brothers. Adaptational Villainy: Hades in the myths is one of the more decent Greek gods and in the comics, while he can be an antagonist, he isn't usually so much a villain as sometimes an obstacle to Wonder Woman. In this adaptation, Hades betrayed the Gods during the Great War to the Titans by giving them a direct entrance to Olympus, but the Gods prevailed and Zeus punished Hades severely for this betrayal - casting him into the Pit of Tartarus where he would rule over the dead for all eternity. Ambiguous Situation: It's not clear whether or not he was lying about being Diana's father. Diana never bothered to confirm it despite Shayera's suggestion of using the Lasso of Truth on him. That being said, it's heavily implied that he wasn't; Diana's interactions with Hermes earlier in the episode, particularly his remark about how Diana is "practically part of the family" along with Diana's black hair (in contrast to her mother's blonde hair) are all hints that heavily suggest it. Archnemesis Dad: He claims to be Wonder Woman's father and he's one of her greatest enemies. Diana hates him and doesn't bother to confirm if he's telling the truth since she doesn't think it matters.

characters.name: Circe
characters.description: Circe was an incredibly powerful sorceress who was banished to Tartarus by Hippolyta, for transforming innocent people into animals. Adaptational Heroism: Circe in the DCAU comes across more as a mischievous, albeit dangerous, magical nuisance rather than a truly genocidal threat. Sure, her comic book counterpart (due to theever-shifting creative team) has occasionally shownsomesympathetic traits, but she was typically up tofarworse things than just randomly transfiguring people and objects for laughs. In the comics, she’s known for engineering full-scale wars between gods and mortals or attempting global genocide (such as the infamousWar of the Godsstoryline). Furthermore, simply talking her into undoing her magic spells was rarely,if ever, an option; heroes usually had to beat her in combat or cleverly outsmart her immense divine ego to break her spell. Affably Evil: Her only on-screen act of villainy is transforming Wonder Woman into a pigto spite Hippolyta. Circe spends the majority of her episode simply pursuing her dream of becoming a professional singer, and by the end of it, not only does she willingly reverse her spell, but she is also shown to be on somewhat friendly terms with Batman and Zatanna. Even Evil Has Standards: Batman strikes a bargain with Circe in a bid to save Wonder Woman, and after seeing Batman hold up his end of the deal, Circe honors their agreement and undoes her curse. Evil Is Hammy: Circe tries to do this. Zatanna doesn't let her.Circe:Insolent trickster! You dare to strike...[hit with a chair]You dare to strike...[hit with a table]You dare to strike...[is covered with a tablecloth, yanks it off]QUIT IT!Oh no...[slammed by a piano]

characters.name: Aresia
characters.description: A woman adopted by the Amazons as a young girl after washing ashore on Themyscira when her boat was destroyed by raiders after fleeing from her wartorn home with her mother. Her experience has caused her to develop a hatred of men, strong enough to want to purge them from the world. Adaptational Karma: Inverted. In an issue of the tie-in comic (which are not canon to the series)Flash, does her a favor after she is defeated, having her be sent to an all-women prison, which she relishes in. This in contrast to the show where she got a well deserved beating from Wonder Woman then was killed when the plane she wanted to use to expose the men-killer allergen to the world and kill men explodes with her inside. Ultimately, this is downplayed because in the comics, she didn't try to destroy all the men in the world but rather control them, and she seems to be genuinely letting go of some of her hatred towards men by being grateful towards the Flash for sending her to an all women's prison. Adaptational Nice Guy: Downplayed in the tie comics of Justice League. She is still a man-hater villain but she switches her plan fromgendercideto just control all the men of the world. Still bad? Yeah. Less horrible than killing every male in the planet? Hell yeah. She also seems to be moreAffably Evilthan her appearance in the series, as she has some friendly chats with Flash and is not as aggressive as she is in the cartoon. Adaptational Villainy: She's loosely based on the heroines who're codenamed "Fury" (referenced by theepisode title)—only as a gendericidal villainess. Alas, Poor Villain: After Aresia is killed, Hippolyta and Diana lament her death as this.

characters.name: Morgaine Le Fey
characters.description: Morgaine le Fey was a powerful and evil sorceress hailing from Arthurian times. Her one goal is to put her son, Mordred, on the throne of Camelot (and by extension, the world) - a quest that she had worked ceaselessly for centuries to fulfill. She hid her true features behind an exquisite mask. Age Without Youth: She wears a mask to hide her time-ravaged face. Arch-Enemy: To Jason Blood and Etrigan. She seduced Jason into opening the gates to Camelot to her army then poisoned for outliving his usefulness. As he lay dying, Merlin bound the demon Etrigan to Jason, forcing him to live and atone for his actions by defeating Morgaine le Fey, a task they've since been at for millennia. Didn't Think This Through: She never anticipated that keeping Mordred a child for centuries while filling his head with dreams of world domination, would lead to Mordred resenting her for smothering him and turning on her the second he gets his hands on an amulet that makes him more powerful than her. Enemy Mine: Helps the Justice League defeat her son, Mordred, when he uses aMacGuffinto banish all the adults in the world to another dimension.

characters.name: Mordred
characters.description: Morgaine le Fey's son. Alas, Poor Villain: Given that Mordred was magically trapped as a child for millennia by his smothering mother, never being allowed to grow up or mature, it's hard not to pity his ultimate fate when he breaks his mother's spell. Though he no longer has eternal youth, he still has eternal life, and he rapidly ages into a catatonic old man who now has to rely on his mother to take care of him forever. Anti-Villain: Downplayed, given he wants to rule the world, but he's not actually malevolent and does want to beThe Good Kingand is even seen taking requests from his subjects - despite being clearly bored - when he briefly ruled the world in "Kids' Stuff." He also has aMy God, What Have I Done?moment when he makes one of his "subjects" cry. Even with all the power of the Amulet of First Magic flowing through him, he was ultimately just a spoiled kid who actually has the power to enact whatever whims he has, with all that comes with that,Didn't Think This Throughincluded. Didn't Think This Through: Kid Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, and Green Lantern trick him into magically aging himself into an adult. Mordred doesn't realize that this makes him susceptible to the same spell he cast that banishes all adults to a shadow dimension. He also doesn't think through the long term consequences of breaking a spell that keeps him young forever. Even Evil Has Standards: Though he aspires to take over the world, Mordred isn't pure evil, just a spoiled child that doesn't think things through. Even after banishing all adults on Earth to a shadow dimension so he can rule, he still shows discomfort and guilt over making a little girl cry.

characters.name: Felix Faust
characters.description: Felix Faust was a practitioner of dark magic, a pursuit that cost him his university teaching job, and, ultimately, his soul. Alliterative Name:FelixFaust. Asshole Victim:Considering his desire for power and cruelty towards other people, nobody feels sorry when Hades claims his soul and says he'll spend the next few millennia torturing him. Big Ol' Eyebrows: He has large eyebrows. Bond Villain Stupidity: Despite being powerful enough just to kill Wonder Woman and Shayera, instead he sends them to a different level of Tartarus. The very same one where he's keeping Hades, who they're able to free and ally with in order to defeat Faust.

characters.name: Shadow Thief
characters.description: A thief with shadow powers who targets archaeological sites and treasures. He is later revealed to be the living embodiment of the dark side of Carter Hall, AKA, Hawkman. Adaptational Badass: There have been multiple Shadow Thieves in the comics but all of them relied on technology for their powers. In this adaptation, Shadow Thief, while born of Thanagarian technology (and / or magic), is a living psychic projection capable of outright defeating the likes of Green Lantern, Batman and Hawkgirl amongst others in single combat. Adaptational Species Change: In the comics, he was a human thief named Carl Sands who can transform into aLiving Shadowwith an alien-made suit. Casting a Shadow: He has formidable shadow powers that allow him to alter his size and shape, turn his limbs into shadow weapons, hide in shadows, and travel through walls amongst other abilities. Composite Character: Technically, as this version is Carter Hall's dark side instead of Carl Sands or Carl Hammer.

characters.name: The Ophidians
characters.description: A race of humanoid snake beings that worshipped the moon and darkness. Thousands of years ago they battled humans for dominion over the earth thousands of years ago and were nearly wiped out. The survivors performed a ritual during a lunar eclipse that sent their souls into a gem called the Heart of Darkness, allowing them to possess whomever held it and seek vengeance against mankind. Adaptational Backstory Change: The Heart of Darkness in the comics was designed to containEclipso, the former embodiment of God's wrath and angel of vengeance before their power corrupted them. In this continuity, it's instead the vessel of snake people, with Eclipso only referenced when GeneralMcCormickdressed as him when he was possessed by the Ophidians. Adaptational Wimp: Eclipso, or at least the entities within the Heart of Darkness, can possess people, but are not the powerful embodiment of God's wrath who can corrupt, manipulate weather and rival gods like in the comics. Artifact of Doom: The souls of their last handful inhabit a jewel called the Heart of Darkness. Anybody who touches it becomes possessed by one of the Ophidians, whose only goal is toKill All Humansout of vengance for their own kind's extinction. Last of His Kind: The Ophidians who sealed their souls inside the Heart of Darkness were the last of their kind.

characters.name: Lord Orm
characters.description: Lord Orm wasAquaman's villainous younger brother. Adaptational Villainy: He's a far cry from Ocean Master, his comic book counterpart. Not only does he have no real motivation for his resentment towards surface life other thanunbridled bigotry(the comic iteration was ahuman himself, growing jealous of his half-brother's powers), but he has no qualmskilling a baby. Ain't Too Proud to Beg:During his final fight with Aquaman a bridge collapses from underneath him. He begs to be rescued, but Aquaman leaves him to die. Arc Villain: For "The Enemy Below". Aristocrats Are Evil: He's referred to as Lord Orm in the show and certainly doesn't lack the evil part.

characters.name: Icthultu
characters.description: The most powerful ofthe Old Ones, who was once worshipped as a god on Thanagar and tried to break out into Earth from his dimension, alongside the other Old Ones. Cthu-Lookalike: Icthultu is a Thanagarian deity who was sealed away by an Atlantean king when it attempted to attack Earth in the distant past. Icthultu was originally meant tobeCthulhu, butDwayne McDuffiewas unsure if the name had any trademark or copyright associated with it, unaware that Cthulhu was a public domain property. Deal with the Devil: Icthultu taught the Thanagarians agriculture, mathematics and philosophy in the early days of their culture, but in exchange for worship and sacrifices. Eventually the Thanagarians got tired of the high cost of his "help" and rebelled. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: Icthultu questions Hawkgirl on why her people stopped worshipping him after he "gave them everything", and he's genuinely perplexed when she tells him sacrificing her peoples' souls to him was too high a price for his "favors".Icthultu:My tribute was equitable. I earned your faith.Hawkgirl:Really? What's a fair price for the souls of my ancestors?! Lovecraft Lite: As an Old One from another dimension, Icthulhu is certainly a menacing threat, but he's been successfully repelled twice in the past and his encounter with the Justice League and Grundy ultimately result in his defeat and death.

characters.name: Mordru
characters.description: A Lord of Chaos of such apocalyptic magical power that the entire Justice League is dispatched to stop him. All save Booster Gold, who's put on crowd control. Generic Doomsday Villain: He's an evil rampaging sorcerer who threatens to destroy the world but he's given no history, motivation or even characterization. He just randomly appears as a silent force of destruction with even his status as a Lord of Chaos never explained onscreen. This is all intentional given that his presence is more of a backdrop for Booster Gold's story. No Ontological Inertia: The effects of his magic go away once he loses consciousness. Remember the New Guy?: J'onn reacts to Mordru's presence like he's a well-established villain despite "The Greatest Story Never Told" being his debut appearance. Villain of Another Story: Of "The Greatest Story Never Told". The entire joke of his character is that he's a world-ending threat that requires the combined might of the entire Justice League to stop, but their epic battle for the fate of the world is relegated to the B-plot of Booster Gold's story as he tries to save the world from a completely separate apocalypse. Booster never faces him directly and he ends up defeated offscreen byElongated Manwho was the only other hero besides Booster to be initially left out of the fight.

characters.name: A.M.A.Z.O.
characters.description: A.M.A.Z.O., better known simply as The Android or Professor Ivo's Android, was a nanotechnogical creation of the late Professor Ivo. Amazo's nanotechnology enabled him to copy any trait and characteristic of people and objects, by merely looking at them. Adaptive Ability: He was able to take Superman's powers and then overcome hisKryptonite Factorafter exposure to kryptonite, and his own nanotech weaknesses which causes Luthor's only weapon against him to fail. Adaptational Badass: Mainstream Amazo is by no means a pushover but even the strongest version of Amazo in the comics is limited toPower Copying. He can use all of the abilities of the superbeings he encounters (barring magic) and use themall at onceinstead ofone at a time. Here Amazo has that plus an adaptive ability that lets him constantly change, evolve, gain new abilities, and grow beyond his weaknesses. Mainsteam Amazo is at best aPhysical Godbut here he is a straight upReality Warper. All-Powerful Bystander: After his return to Earth, he spent some time at Dr. Fate's retreat, but theRule of Dramadictated that his immense powers had to be useless against the first entity he tried to help the League with - at which point he departed and was never seen again. Adaptational Nice Guy: Comics Amazo is more or lessThe Bruteno matter the incarnation, a powerful servant android to whoever is his current master. This Amazo is an introspective and childlike creature that tries to avoid escalation and never goes out of his way to hurt people,thankfully.

characters.name: Brimstone
characters.description: A war machine developed in Chong-Mai that went rogue. All There in the Manual: Its name is Brimstone, but it's never referred to as such onscreen, only in a DVD featurette. Achilles' Heel: The only way to defeat it is to lodge a carbon rod into the small exposed hole under its head. Adaptational Backstory Change: Brimstone goes from being Darkseid's creation to an invention of the Chong-Mai government. Gone Horribly Wrong: Brimstone was built to protect the country of Chong-Mai from foreigners, but somehow it went haywire and started killing indiscriminately.

characters.name: Emerald Empress
characters.description: A woman in possession of the Emerald Eye of Ekron. Alliterative Name:EmeraldEmpress. Ax-Crazy: After escaping Oa, she wants to destroy Earth to change history so the Legion of Superheroes never exists. Badass Cape: She wears one that's black on the outside, green on the inside. Badass in Distress: She's being held in maximum confinement on present-day Oa.

characters.name: Tharok
characters.description: A man who is half-human and half-machine, quite literally physically and in personality. Bald of Evil: He's a bald supervillain. Cyborg:Vertically,with his left side being machine. In the source material, this was because the left half of his body gotvaporized, but the people of his homeworld managed to save him with cybernetics. Deadpan Snarker: While complaining about rescuing Emerald Empress, he asks how she and Mano can even work if the latter can't useone of his hands. Evil Genius: Thanks to half of his brain being a computer. InVs. The Fatal Five, it turns into the question of who's smarter, him or Mr. Terrific, who is said by Batman to maybe be the third smartest man on Earth.

characters.name: The Persuader
characters.description: A man wielding an axe that can cut through just about anything. Absurdly Sharp Blade: Justified. His axe has been cut to less than a nanometer thick, supposedly allowing it to cut through almost anything, including Superman's skin, a Green Lantern ring, and the force of gravity itself. Brutish Character, Brutish Weapon: A viciousBlood Knightwho carries an axe that can cut anything. He manages to slice open Superman, leaving him a bloody mess, and manages to cut apart a Green Lantern Ring. Blood Knight: Is the most vicious fighter of the Five. When in present day, he opined if he could be the reason the Green Lantern Corps is no longer a thing in the 31st Century. Deadpan Snarker:Green Arrow:[clashing his bow against Persuader's axe while Persuader has him cornered]Just so you know, the sharp thing's on the other end.The Persuader:Yeah, don't worry, that part's coming.

characters.name: Mano
characters.description: A mutant with the "anti-matter touch" — the power to disintegrate anything he touches with his right hand. After using his touch to destroy his homeworld, he became an outlaw and joined the Fatal Five. Ascended Extra: InVs. The Fatal Five, he's the group's temporary leader while Emerald Empress is out of commission, whereas in "Far From Home", he had no lines and was greatly overshadowed by his colleagues (he only had under a minute of screentime). Cop Hater: As a super-criminal, he at one point insults theGreen Lantern Corpsby calling them the "Green Fascist Corps". Death by Looking Up: When Mano watches Jessica Cruz dropping the whole cave on top of him and is crushed along with the rest of the team. The Dragon: He leads Tharok and the Persuader while Emerald Empress is out of action. Not that any of the three of them are harmless on their own...

characters.name: Validus
characters.description: A mindless brute with incredible strength, strong enough to match Superman's. Adapted Out: One of the most iconic parts of the character is thathe’s actually the son of founding Legionnaires Lightning Lad and Saturn Girl, with Darkseid kidnapping him and transforming him into a monster. This is never brought up at any point, although it can be seen asjustifiedthanks toDarkseid being permanently absorbed into the Source Wall in “Destroyer”, long before the Legion of Superheroes or the Fatal Five were ever formed. Attack Its Weak Point: Can stand toe to toe with Superman, but damaging the glass casing protecting his brain is enough to cause him great pain. Dumb Muscle: Is little more than the Empress's attack dog. Irony: Has an exposed brain andPsychic Powers...and is a mindless beast.

characters.name: Captain Cold
characters.description: A crook from Central City who specializes in performing heists with his cold guns. Henpecked Husband: Captain Cold mentions that his wife will have him bagging groceries if he can't make the mortgage with supervillainy. Captain Boomerang says she always was an ice queen. An Ice Person: Captain Cold wields guns that shoots ice and is capable of freezing people alive. Non-Member in the Adaptation: Captain Cold, a member of the original Legion of Doom, is not a member of its equivalent—the Secret Society—in this version. Interestingly, he's the only example with no reason, with the Riddler, the Scarecrow, and Black Manta being under Embargo, Grundy being dead, and (depending on your view) Brainiac no longer having a body. Even more strange considering Mirror Master is a member.

characters.name: The Trickster
characters.description: A supervillain from Central City who's one of Flash's rogues. He's not an evil man, just one suffering from a mental illness, so he isn't treated as a true villain by the Flash. Anti-Villain: He's only a villain because he thinks it's fun due to his mental illness. Flash deals with him by talking to him and asking him to turn himself in afterwards. Disabled in the Adaptation: The Trickster is a sane criminal in the comics. Here, he's so out of touch with reality, it takes the Flash pointing out that he's in the costume to realize that he's indeed wearing it. Drug-Crazed Savagery: Inverted with the Trickster going on one of his supervillain sprees after cutting down on his medications. Flash tells him, inSincerity Mode, that he has to take them regularly to make them work. Even Evil Has Standards: He was iffy about playing darts in a hospital until the Flash assured him he'd get "the soft kind."

characters.name: Vandal Savage
characters.description: A man who has existed for eons due to his interactions with a mysterious meteor that landed on Earth. He is an intellectual genius and a master strategist who can account for numerous outcomes due to his long life. Like many of his ilk, he thirsts for power and being nigh-immortal, is aware that once he has it he will be undisputed for eternity. Adaptational Heroism: Vandal Savage is one of the most evil characters in the DC universe in the comics. This incarnation seems to follow suituntil "Hereafter" where he makes aHeel–Face Turnafter causing the apocalypse. Age Lift: He's still a caveman who became immortal through the radiation of a meteor, but this happened 25,000 years ago, half the time it happened in the comics. The Aloner: In "Hereafter"he's left the last living human on Earth after one of his mad bids for power caused the apocalypse, leaving him alone in a wasteland populated by mutated animals and no sapient life. The ensuing millennia has resulted in him being eaten away by guilt over what he's done, and though he tells Superman that it would be simple for him to travel into space to seek out other life, he willingly remains in self-imposed exile on Earth as penance for his crimes. Arc Villain: He's the villain for the three-parter finale of the first season "The Savage Time" and the two-parter "Maid of Honor". In "Hereafter" it's revealed he'sresponsible for the apocalypse that killed everyone on Earth, but by the time he meets and confesses to a time-displaced Superman, he's stopped being a villain and instead helps Superman undo his past deeds.

characters.name: Solomon Grundy
characters.description: Solomon Grundy was a zombie created when a criminal by the name of Cyrus Gold was killed in a swamp outside Gotham City. Age Lift: The Cryus Gold of the comics was a 19th century merchant before dying and becoming Grundy. Here, pre-Grundy Gold was a Prohibition-era gangster. Asshole Victim: His living self, Cyrus Gold, was this, being a vicious gangster who killed many innocent people and ultimately died pushing his luck with dangerous men. It doesn't really apply to Grundy himself, as he's a separate entity created by Cyrus' corpse being cursed and thrown into a magic swamp. Berserk Button: Upon hearing that Icthultu eats souls, he rips a hole through its body and then charges all by himself towards its brain, crushing all the defenders in his way. The Brute: He's the dumb muscle for whichever supervillain has hired him this week.

characters.name: Ultra-Humanite
characters.description: Ultra-Humanite was an albino gorilla-humanoid whose intelligence is far superior to most men. Unfortunately, his true talents were not put to use when he served as a member of the Injustice Gang. Adaptational Late Appearance: He debuted in the comics before Lex Luthor did, and originated as the first recurring enemy of Superman prior to the Post-Crisis canon changing him to fighting the Justice Society in general decades before Superman entered the picture. In this continuity he makes his first appearance long after Lex Luthor's debut and with no indication that he's been active nearly as long as his comic book incarnation. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the comics, Ultra-Humanite is aCard-Carrying Villainwho is despicable enough to engineer a highly contagious and life-threatening plague, as well as cheat death by stealing an innocent woman's body to transplant his brain into. In this adaptation, he's anAnti-Villainwho only wants what he thinks is best for humanity's cultural values, and is willing to help the Flash ensure the children at an orphanage have a good Christmas despite his initial disdain for the holiday. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: In the comics, Ultra-Humanite was Superman’sArch-Enemyin the earliest years of the comic and debuted before even Lex Luthor did. In the DCAU, he never appeared inSuperman’s own show, and was never shown antagonizing Superman before the Justice League was formed. Even after that, the two didn’t cross paths very often. Affably Evil: He doesn't enjoy civilian casualties in the least. And he's also more than willing to help the Flash withspreading some Christmas cheer for orphan kids.

characters.name: Chronos
characters.description: David Clinton was a small time physics professor from the future Gotham City who developed the technology to travel in time as Chronos. Adaptational Badass: This Chronos is way more powerful than his comic book counterpart fromThe DCU. Age Lift: Technically, as the comics David Clinton was a present-day character. This version is from the era ofBatman Beyond, which would make him a kid at most in the present. And I Must Scream: AFreeze-Frame Bonusat the end of his two-parter shows he's aware of hisTime Loop Trapand is unable to do anything to stop it. Arc Villain: Of "The Once and Future Thing".

characters.name: Bloodsport II
characters.description: A villain in Gotham City. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the comics, the white Bloodsport was awhite supremacist. This one is a crazyConspiracy Theoristwith no indication that he's racist or otherwise discriminatory. Adaptational Wimp: In the comics Bloodsport II was a muscular killer with a large array of weaponry who managed to rack up a lot of victims. This version is a scrawny nutjob who lacks a real arsenal and fails to kill anyone, and just resorts to making threats. Composite Character: He uses the costume and weapons of the first Bloodsport (RobertDuBois), but is Caucasian like the Alex Trent version. Conspiracy Theorist: He's a terrorist who believes John F. Kennedy faked his assassination attempt and threatens to kill innocent people if Kennedy doesn't show himself and admit "the truth".

characters.name: Simon Stagg
characters.description: The corrupt head of Stagg Industries and the man responsible for the creation of Metamorpho. Alliterative Name:SimonStagg. Big Ol' Eyebrows: He’s got the same big, evil-looking eyebrows as his mainstream counterpart. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He presents a friendly, charismatic front to investors and valued employees, but, if challenged, it can easily give way to the ruthless corporate ghoul lurking beneath. The only person who he doesn't let his mask of affability slip around is his daughter but even then it's strongly implied he has sinister motives for that as well. Boyfriend-Blocking Dad: Rex Mason and Sapphire hid their relationship from him because of Stagg's well-documented belief that "No one's too good for Simon Stagg's little girl." When they finally tell him about their relationship and that Sapphire is leaving him to join Rex in Chicago, Stagg decides to use Rex as a test subject for his Metamorpho experiment.

characters.name: Morgan Edge
characters.description: Morgan Edge was a black market collector. Adaptational Wimp: He was at one point the leader of Intergang in the comics. This incarnation is just an eccentric billionaire who ends up getting killed. Asshole Victim: He's a black market collector who acquired Clayface and kept him trapped as part of his collection. He's hardly missed when Killer Frost decides to live up to her name. Collector of the Strange: He addedClayfaceto his collection. Death by Adaptation: Morgan Edge remained alive and well in the comics, while this incarnation is heavily implied to end up frozen to death by Killer Frost.

characters.name: Steven Mandragora
characters.description: Steven Mandragora was a powerful crime boss who had once murdered the parents of a young Helena Bertinelli, who becameHuntressin an attempt to track him down and kill him in revenge. Badass in a Nice Suit: He wears a pretty awesome suit while kickingBlack Canary's butt. Batman Gambit: He's aware that he can't carry out his plans as long as Green Arrow and Black Canary are around keeping an eye on him, so he acts even more repulsive than usual to wind the two of them up until one of them strikes him, ensuring they'll get kicked out of his house, giving him the perfect opportunity to make his escape from the feds keeping him there. Charles Atlas Superpower: Approaching this, if not already there. Composite Character: His name and role as the one who killed Huntress's parents comes from Stefano Mandragora, but his appearance and abilities are based more on Tobias Whale.

characters.name: G. Gordon Godfrey
characters.description: Not a supervillain, just aJerkasstalkshow host who slanders the League to boost his ratings. Adaptation Species Change: In the comics, Gordon Godfrey is ahuman alienknown as a New God named Glorious Godfrey from the planet Apokolips. Here, as far as we see, he's just a regular human. Adaptational Nice Guy: Downplayed. While it's difficult to say how far he'd go before hitting any sort of standard due to his limited screentime... It's highly unlikely that he's as depraved as the comics version of Glorious Godfrey, a willing acolyte of Darkseid. Adaptational Wimp: He's usually a New God named Glorious Godfrey in disguise, which doesn't seem to be the case here. Blatant Lies: After the Justice League saves the world and becomes popular again (which causes Godfrey tolosehispopularity, and his sponsors), Godfrey makes a vain attempt to salvage his reputation by claiming he only criticized the Justice Leaue because he cares.
